legal.privacy.title: Privacy policy
legal.terms.title: Terms of service
legal.privacy.intro: Sessional is software that schools and conference organisers (“schools”) use to run Model United Nations conferences. It is operated by {operator} (“we”). This policy explains what we keep about people who use it, why, and what you can ask of us. Questions: {email}.
legal.privacy.s1.title: Schools decide, we process
legal.privacy.s1.body: Each school decides who is invited, what is entered about its participants and how long it is kept. For that information the school is responsible (the “controller”); we keep and process it only to provide Sessional to the school, on its instructions. Many participants are students under 18: the school is responsible for any consent needed from them or their parents under the laws that apply to it.
legal.privacy.s2.title: What we keep
legal.privacy.s2.body:
• Accounts: name, email address, the schools a person belongs to, their role and status, and when they chose a password or signed in. Passwords are stored by our authentication provider as one-way hashes; we never see them.
• Conference records a school enters: committees, chairs, delegations (usually a country, sometimes a delegate's name), attendance, speakers, motions, votes, warnings, documents, grades, notes and awards.
• Settings a school chooses: its name, design, logo, texts, rules and an access code (kept only as a one-way hash).
• An audit log of changes (who changed what and when), kept for the school's own oversight.
• Technical records needed to run and protect the service (for example the time of a request and whether it succeeded). We do not put names or email addresses in these records.
legal.privacy.s3.title: How we use it
legal.privacy.s3.body: Only to provide Sessional to schools: to sign people in, show each person what their role allows, run sessions, keep grades and produce the files a school downloads, and to keep the service secure. We do not sell personal information, show advertising, build profiles of people, or use tracking or analytics cookies.
legal.privacy.s4.title: Google user data
legal.privacy.s4.body:
When you choose “Continue with Google”, Sessional asks Google only for the basic sign-in scopes: openid, email and profile.
• Data we receive: your Google account's email address, whether Google has verified it, your name, and Google's identifier for your account.
• How we use it: only to sign you in to the schools that invited you, to match you with the invitation sent to that address, and to show your name to the people you work with in Sessional.
• How we store it: in our authentication and database provider (Supabase), encrypted in transit; we keep no Google access or refresh tokens after sign-in.
• Sharing: we do not share, sell or transfer Google user data to anyone, except our hosting providers as needed to run the service, or where the law requires it. We do not use it for advertising, and no person reads it except to give support you ask for.
• Retention and deletion: it is kept while your account exists. Ask your school or write to {email} to delete it; you can also remove Sessional's access at any time from your Google Account (Security → Your connections to third-party apps).
• Sessional's use and transfer of information received from Google APIs adheres to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.
Sign-in with Microsoft works the same way: we receive only your name, email address and whether it is verified, and use them only to sign you in.
legal.privacy.s5.title: Who else handles it
legal.privacy.s5.body:
• Within a school, information is visible according to the roles the school sets; one school never sees another school's information.
• Our service providers, only to run Sessional: Supabase (database, authentication and file storage) and Vercel (hosting). They act on our instructions under their own data-protection terms.
• Authorities, only where the law requires it.
legal.privacy.s6.title: Cookies
legal.privacy.s6.body: Sessional uses only cookies it needs to work: keeping you signed in (s_at, s_rt), remembering your language (s_lang), remembering that you entered a school's access code (s_gate), pairing a projection screen (s_screen_…), completing a Google or Microsoft sign-in (s_pkce) and showing an editor their unpublished changes (s_preview). There are no advertising or analytics cookies.
legal.privacy.s7.title: How long we keep it
legal.privacy.s7.body: As long as the school uses Sessional, or until the school removes it. A school can remove people and records at any time. When a school closes its account we delete its information within 90 days; backups are overwritten within a further 30 days.
legal.privacy.s8.title: Security
legal.privacy.s8.body: Connections are encrypted. Each school's information is separated from every other school's in the database itself, and access inside a school follows the roles it sets. Secrets stay on our servers. We keep as little as the service needs.
legal.privacy.s9.title: Your choices and rights
legal.privacy.s9.body: You can ask to see, correct or delete information about you. Because schools decide what they keep, please ask your school first; you can also write to {email} and we will help or pass your request to the school. Depending on where you live you may also have the right to complain to a data-protection authority.
legal.privacy.s10.title: Children
legal.privacy.s10.body: Sessional is meant to be used by schools, under their supervision. Children do not sign up on their own: a school invites them. If you believe a child's information was entered without the permission it needed, write to {email} and we will work with the school to remove it.
legal.privacy.s11.title: Changes
legal.privacy.s11.body: We will update this policy when what we do changes, and show the date at the top. Important changes are announced to schools before they apply.
legal.terms.intro: These terms apply to everyone who uses Sessional, operated by {operator} (“we”). By using Sessional you accept them. If you use it for a school, you accept them on the school's behalf and confirm you may do so.
legal.terms.s1.title: The service
legal.terms.s1.body: Sessional helps schools run Model United Nations conferences: committees, sessions, voting, grades, screens and the school's own site. It is still being built; features may change, and some are marked as coming later.
legal.terms.s2.title: Accounts
legal.terms.s2.body: Accounts are created by invitation from a school. Keep your password and any access code to yourself and tell your school if you think someone else used them. You are responsible for what is done with your account.
legal.terms.s3.title: What schools agree to
legal.terms.s3.body:
• Enter only information they are allowed to, and obtain any consent needed from participants or their parents.
• Give people the roles they need and no more (for example, not giving students staff permissions unless intended).
• Keep their information accurate and remove it when it is no longer needed.
legal.terms.s4.title: Acceptable use
legal.terms.s4.body: Do not use Sessional to break the law, harass anyone or share harmful content; do not try to reach another school's information, get around permissions or access codes, overload the service, or test its security without our written permission.
legal.terms.s5.title: Your content
legal.terms.s5.body: Schools own what they enter. They give us permission to store and process it only to provide Sessional to them. They can download it, and delete it, at any time.
legal.terms.s6.title: Availability
legal.terms.s6.body: We work to keep Sessional available and secure, but it is provided “as is”, without guarantees that it will always be available or free of errors. Keep your own copies of anything you cannot do without.
legal.terms.s7.title: Liability
legal.terms.s7.body: To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for indirect or consequential losses, or for losses caused by misuse of an account or by information a school entered. Nothing in these terms limits liability that cannot be limited by law.
legal.terms.s8.title: Suspension and ending
legal.terms.s8.body: We may suspend access that breaks these terms or puts others at risk, telling the school when we can. A school may stop using Sessional at any time; its information is then deleted as described in the privacy policy.
legal.terms.s9.title: Changes and law
legal.terms.s9.body: We may update these terms and will show the date at the top; important changes are announced to schools first. These terms are governed by the law of {country}.
legal.terms.s10.title: Contact

landing.step.rollcall.title: Roll call
landing.step.rollcall.body: Present, present and voting, absent. Quorum and the majorities needed for the session are worked out as delegations answer.
landing.step.speakers.title: Speakers list and timer
landing.step.speakers.body: Add delegations in the order placards go up, set the speaking time, yield to the chair, to questions or to another delegate. The timer sounds and flashes when time runs out.
landing.step.motions.title: Motions and points
landing.step.motions.body: Moderated and unmoderated caucuses, extensions, closing debate. Motions are ranked by how disruptive they are, so the chair votes on them in the right order.
landing.step.documents.title: Working papers and resolutions
landing.step.documents.body: Delegations submit, the chair approves and numbers them, amendments are tracked against the draft, and the passed resolution can be printed in the committee's format.
landing.step.voting.title: Voting
landing.step.voting.body: By placard, by roll call or in secret, with abstentions and vetoes where the committee has them. If the Wi-Fi drops mid-vote, the votes wait on the laptop and are sent when it is back.
landing.step.after.title: Grades and awards
landing.step.after.body: Chairs grade against your rubric during the session. Awards are worked out from your rules, and certificates come out ready to print with each delegate's name and flag.
landing.screens.title: Three screens in the room
landing.screens.intro: The chair's console is one of them. The other two follow it without anyone touching them.
landing.screens.projector: The projector shows who is speaking, the time left and who is next. Pair it once with a short code; it reconnects by itself.
landing.screens.phone: Delegates see their committee on their phone, with no account and no app to install.
landing.screens.placard: Placards print with the flag and a code for check-in at the door.
landing.organisers.title: For the people organising it
landing.organisers.intro: What the Secretariat and the staff behind it use before, during and after the conference.
landing.org.import.title: Bring your spreadsheet
landing.org.import.body: Import committees, countries and delegates from Excel, CSV or a Google Sheet, every tab at once. Rows with problems are listed with the reason, and an import can be undone.
landing.org.schedule.title: Schedule
landing.org.schedule.body: Sessions, breaks and ceremonies, shown to everyone in their own time zone.
landing.org.analytics.title: Every committee at a glance
landing.org.analytics.body: Which committees are in session, who is speaking, how many delegations answered roll call, and where a chair needs help.
landing.org.print.title: Printing
landing.org.print.body: Placards, sign-in sheets, the agenda, resolutions, grade reports and certificates, as PDFs in your conference's colours.
landing.org.grading.title: Grading
landing.org.grading.body: Your own rubric, categories and weights. A chair can only see their own committee's grades. Exports to CSV, Excel or PDF in the columns your school asks for.
landing.org.documents.title: Documents
landing.org.documents.body: Position papers and resolutions stored with the committee, with a record of who changed what.
landing.org.people.title: People and roles
landing.org.people.body: Invite chairs and staff by email; sign in with Google or Microsoft. Students on the Secretariat get what they need for the event and nothing more.
landing.org.audit.title: A log of every change
landing.org.audit.body: Each admin action is recorded with who did it and when, and staff can read the log.
landing.org.access.title: Announcements
landing.org.access.body: Post a notice to every committee screen at once, or only to one.
landing.org.history.title: Last year, cloned
landing.org.history.body: Start next year's conference from this year's in one step, and compare the two years side by side.
landing.org.export.title: Your data leaves with you
landing.org.export.body: Export everything as JSON, CSV or PDF at any time. An export imports back into an empty conference with the same counts.
landing.org.public.title: A public page
landing.org.public.body: Committees, topics and the schedule on a public page you choose the fields for. Confidential crisis topics stay hidden until you open them.
landing.yours.title: Your conference, your words
landing.yours.intro: Nothing about Sessional's own name or colours has to show to your delegates.
landing.yours.look.title: Your look
landing.yours.look.body: Logo, colours and fonts, with a preview before anything goes live. Colours that would be hard to read are corrected for contrast.
landing.yours.site.title: Your address
landing.yours.site.body: Each school has its own address, like yourschool.sessional.app, with its own sign-in page.
landing.yours.rules.title: Your rules of procedure
landing.yours.rules.body: Start from UN, Harvard, THIMUN or the Spanish reglamento and change what your conference does differently.
landing.yours.types.title: Your kinds of committee
landing.yours.types.body: General assemblies, security councils with vetoes, crisis cabinets, press corps, courts. Each kind has its own fields and rules.
landing.yours.languages.title: English, Spanish, and more
landing.yours.languages.body: Every screen comes in English and Spanish. Add another language yourself, including right-to-left ones such as Arabic, and country names follow.
landing.students.title: Most of the people using it are students
landing.students.intro: So it keeps as little about them as it can, and the adults keep control.
landing.students.accounts: Delegates don't need an account to follow their committee.
landing.students.names: Public pages show only the fields you choose. Names, emails and grades are never in a link.
landing.students.staff: Students on the Secretariat can run the event, but cannot change who has access, the billing or delete the conference.
landing.students.log: Every admin action is logged. If our support team ever signs in to help, it needs a reason, shows a banner and appears in your log.
landing.students.least: Each school's data is kept apart from every other school's, and tested that way on every change.
landing.students.export: You can export everything, and delete it.
landing.pricing.title: Pricing
landing.pricing.intro: Per year, per conference or per month. Prices are shown in your currency at checkout, before tax.
landing.pricing.soon: Pricing is being finalised. Write to us and we'll set up your conference.
landing.pricing.notes: Going over a limit never stops a session that is running; you are told and can move up a plan. If a payment fails, your conference stays readable while it is sorted out.
landing.next.title: Coming next
landing.next.intro: Not built yet. These are next, in this order.
landing.next.signup.title: Sign up on your own, with a demo conference
landing.next.signup.body: Create your school's space without writing to us, and start from a sample conference already full of committees and delegates.
landing.next.email.title: Email from your own address, on your own domain
landing.next.email.body: Invitations and notices sent from your conference's address, the site on your own domain, and no Sessional name anywhere on larger plans.
landing.next.gallery.title: A shared gallery
landing.next.gallery.body: Themes, rules of procedure and rubrics that other conferences have published, installed as a draft you can try first.
landing.next.help.title: Help centre and an accessibility audit
landing.next.help.body: Guides for chairs, the Secretariat and faculty advisors, and an outside check against WCAG AA with high-contrast and large-text modes.
landing.faq.title: Questions
landing.faq.accounts.q: Does every delegate need an account?
landing.faq.accounts.a: No. Chairs and staff sign in. Delegates open their committee's page on their phone without one.
landing.faq.wifi.q: What if the Wi-Fi goes down during a vote?
landing.faq.wifi.a: The chair's laptop keeps working. Each action waits until the server has it, and the screen only says saved once it does.
landing.faq.rules.q: Our conference has its own rules. Will it fit?
landing.faq.rules.a: Start from the closest preset and change the motions, majorities, speaking times and vote types to match. The changes are previewed before they go live.
landing.faq.spanish.q: Can delegates use it in Spanish?
landing.faq.spanish.a: Yes. Each person can pick their language, and the conference can choose which languages to offer.
landing.faq.data.q: Who can see our students' grades?
landing.faq.data.a: Only the chairs of that committee and the staff you allow. Other schools on Sessional can never see your data.
landing.faq.cost.q: Can a class try it first?
landing.faq.cost.a: Yes. A class or club simulation fits the smallest plan, and every plan can start with a trial.
landing.footer.made: Sessional, conference software for Model UN.

home.about: Sessional runs Model United Nations conferences for schools: chairs take roll call, manage speakers, motions and votes from a live console; projection screens follow the room; organisers grade delegates and export gradebooks; each school gets its own branded site. Accounts are created by invitation from a school.

landing.start.title: Running a conference this school year?
landing.start.body: Tell us the dates and how many committees. We set up your school's address and bring in your spreadsheet with you, before the first session.
landing.start.bodySignedUp: Schools already on Sessional sign in at their own address, or here.
